title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is Grothendieck's functional equation for L-functions over a finite field, in the case where the variety is not proper. The page treats the 'part at infinity', meaning the defect between the L-functions of Rf_* and Rf_!.

Notation. X is the variety and i: X -> X̄ is an open immersion into a compactification. j: Y -> X̄ is the inclusion of the closed boundary Y = X̄ - X. f is the (proper) structure map of Y, or of X̄, to the base S (here a finite field F_p).

1. Cohomology at infinity. Grothendieck defines R_∞f(E) = Rf_* j^* Ri_*(E). This is the cohomology of the 'punctured tubular neighbourhood at infinity', i.e. boundary or link cohomology. It sits in the triangle Rf_!E -> Rf_*E -> R_∞f(E) ->.

2. Duality computation. Let D be Verdier duality.
- f is proper on Y, so D Rf_* = Rf_* D.
- D j^* = j^! D, and D Ri_* = Ri_! D. He calls these steps 'dualité locale'.
- Hence D R_∞f(E) = Rf_* Rj^! Ri_!(DE).
- He then identifies j^! Ri_!(F) with j^* Ri_*(F) up to a shift. This follows from the triangle j_*j^! i_!F -> i_!F -> Ri_*F, since i^*Ri_* = id.
- Conclusion: D R_∞f(E) ≅ R_∞f(DE)[±1], with the marginal note 'vérifier si c'est 1 ou −1 !'.

3. Self-dual case. Assume X is smooth of relative dimension n and E is lisse and self-dual of weight q, i.e. Ě ≅ E(q). Then DE ≅ Ě(n)[2n] ≅ E(n+q)[2n]. So the boundary complex is self-dual with an odd shift: D R_∞f(E) ≅ R_∞f(E)(n+q)[odd].

4. Functional equation. Write L^∞_E(t) = Π det(1 − Ft | H^i R_∞f E)^{(−1)^{i+1}}. Because the duality shift is odd, the determinant inverts rather than being preserved. This gives a 'product' functional equation
  L^∞_E(1/(p^{n+q} t)) · L^∞_E(t) · (−t)^{χ_∞(E)} · δ_∞(E) = 1,
where χ_∞ is the Euler characteristic of the boundary complex and δ_∞ is a determinant constant. This is unlike the usual quotient form L(1/(p^w t)) ∝ L(t). Here p denotes the cardinality of the finite field and q is the weight.

Purpose: combine this with the duality Rf_! ↔ Rf_* to compare L_E (compact supports) with the L-function of DE, as in the page header 'comparaison ... de L_E et L^∞_{DE}'. It is a bookkeeping step in the Grothendieck–Lefschetz/SGA 5 approach to the functional equation for non-proper varieties.
errors: Shift sign. Grothendieck's boxed formula has [1] and he flagged it himself. Using the triangle j_*j^!i_!F -> i_!F -> Ri_*F gives j^!i_!F ≅ j^*Ri_*F[−1], hence D R_∞f(E) ≅ R_∞f(DE)[−1] with D(K) = RHom(K, Q_l) on a point. Check: X = A^1, boundary a point. R_∞f(Q_l) = Q_l ⊕ Q_l(−1)[−1], so D gives Q_l ⊕ Q_l(1)[1]. Meanwhile R_∞f(DQ_l) = R_∞f(Q_l(1)[2]) = Q_l(1)[2] ⊕ Q_l[1]. The two agree after a shift by −1.
D(E) ≅ Ě(n) omits the shift [2n] for smooth X of dimension n. This is harmless for the L-function, since 2n is even, but is needed for the stated [±1].
Ě ≅ E(q) is an extra hypothesis (self-duality of weight q) that is only implicit; the marginal 'de rang r [?]' is irrelevant to it.

The functional equation is consistent under t -> 1/t: the boxed product form follows from the preceding line. Sanity check on A^1: L^∞(t) = (1−pt)/(1−t) gives L^∞(t)·L^∞(1/(pt)) = p, so δ_∞ = 1/p with χ_∞ = 0.

ideas.what: Cohomology at infinity R_∞f(E) = Rf_* j^* Ri_* E, fitting into Rf_! -> Rf_* -> R_∞f
ideas.modern_name: boundary / link cohomology (cohomology of the punctured neighbourhood of infinity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard. Classical in topology; in étale/ℓ-adic settings used by Harder, Pink (1992, boundary cohomology of Shimura varieties) and others
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in SGA 5 discussions of the functional equation; unsure

ideas.what: Verdier duality for the boundary complex with an odd shift: D R_∞f(E) ≅ R_∞f(DE)[−1]
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré–Verdier duality for link cohomology (the boundary is 'a (2n−1)-manifold')
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore consequence of Verdier duality (Verdier, Grothendieck SGA 4)

ideas.what: Product-type functional equation L^∞(t)·L^∞(1/(p^w t))·(−t)^{χ_∞}·δ_∞ = 1 for the L-function at infinity of a self-dual sheaf
ideas.modern_name: functional equation of boundary L-function / local factor at infinity, from odd-degree self-duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. the Grothendieck functional equation for L-functions (SGA 5, SGA 4½ 'Rapport')

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct (up to the shift sign he flagged himself) derivation of duality for cohomology at infinity and the resulting product-form functional equation. It is natural, folklore-level bookkeeping for the functional equation of L-functions of non-proper varieties, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'R^*_∞ f' in the boxed formulas is probably just R_∞ f (the star may be a stray mark or a superscript distinguishing the version used); the image is ambiguous.
The line 'j^*(Ri_*(D(E)))[1]' is written under a brace beneath Rj^!(Ri_!(D(E))), as its identification; it is not a separate equation.
Header reads roughly 'comparaison générale(?) de L_E et L^∞_{DE}'; 'finale' is uncertain.
'p' in the functional equation denotes the cardinality of the finite field, and 'q' is the weight (Ě ≅ E(q)), not the field size.
